title: He Walked Away With a Limp and a New Name… Then God Said It Again
paragraphs:
He Walked Away With a Limp and a New Name… Then God Said It Again
Why God Didn’t Just Rename Jacob Once—and What That Means for the Parts of You Still Wrestling in Silence
There are moments in life when you think God has already changed you… and yet something inside you still feels unfinished.
Jacob knew that feeling.

He had spent years running from his past—deception clinging to his name like a shadow he couldn’t outrun. His very identity was a scandal. “Jacob” (יַעֲקֹב, Yaʿaqōḇ)—from the Hebrew root ʿaqab, meaning “to supplant,” “to deceive,” “to grasp the heel.” His story began with him gripping his brother’s heel in the womb (Genesis 25:26), as if even then, he was trying to take something that wasn’t his.
And if you’re honest… you’ve had moments like that too. Not necessarily stealing a birthright—but grasping, manipulating, trying to control outcomes because trusting God felt too slow.
But then came that night.
That night when Jacob stopped running.
Genesis 32:24 says, “וַיִּוָּתֵר יַעֲקֹב לְבַדּוֹ… וַיֵּאָבֵק אִישׁ עִמּוֹ” (Vayyivater Yaʿaqōḇ levado… vayyēʾāvēq ish ʿimmō) — “And Jacob was left alone… and a man wrestled with him.”
Alone.
No audience. No excuses. No masks.
Just him… and God.

The Hebrew word “וַיֵּאָבֵק” (vayyēʾāvēq)—“wrestled”—comes from a root that carries the sense of dust being stirred up, like a desperate, gritty struggle in the dirt. This wasn’t a clean, composed prayer. This was messy. Emotional. Raw.
Some of you haven’t had that moment yet. Not fully.
You’ve prayed—but you haven’t wrestled.
Jacob clung to God until his strength gave out. Until his hip was dislocated. Until he physically could not stand the same way again.
And then… God asked him a question that sounds almost strange:
“What is your name?” (Genesis 32:27)
God knew his name.
But Jacob needed to say it.
“Jacob.”
Deceiver.
Supplanter.
Manipulator.
That was his confession.
And then everything changed.
Genesis 32:28: “לֹא יַעֲקֹב יֵאָמֵר עוֹד שִׁמְךָ כִּי אִם־יִשְׂרָאֵל” (Lo Yaʿaqōḇ yeʾamer ʿōd shimkha ki im-Yisraʾel) — “Your name shall no longer be called Jacob, but Israel.”
“Israel” (יִשְׂרָאֵל, Yisraʾel)—“one who strives with God” or “God prevails.”
Not deceiver.
Wrestler.
Chosen.
Transformed.
And yet… years later… God says it again.
Genesis 35:10: “שִׁמְךָ יַעֲקֹב… לֹא־יִקָּרֵא שִׁמְךָ עוֹד יַעֲקֹב כִּי אִם־יִשְׂרָאֵל” — “Your name is Jacob… no longer shall your name be called Jacob, but Israel shall be your name.”
Wait… why repeat it?
Did God forget?
No.
Jacob did.
Because transformation in a moment doesn’t always mean transformation in memory.
God had already renamed him in Genesis 32… but Jacob kept living like Jacob.
He went back to old patterns. Old fears. Old compromises. The name changed—but the habits lagged behind.
And if that doesn’t expose something in us…
How many times has God spoken identity over you—and you still answer to your past?
How many times has grace renamed you—and you still introduce yourself by your failures?
God wasn’t correcting Himself in Genesis 35.
He was reinforcing Jacob.
Because sometimes one encounter with God changes your direction… but repeated reminders are what change your identity.
God met him again at Bethel—the place of promise. Not in crisis this time, but in confirmation.
And this matters more than most people realize.
Because Jacob’s first renaming happened in pain.
The second happened in purpose.
The first was survival.
The second was establishment.
God wasn’t just changing what Jacob had been.
He was anchoring who Jacob would become.
This is where the Gospel begins to breathe into the story.
Because what happened to Jacob didn’t end with Jacob.
Centuries later, another name would be spoken in a quiet, scandal-filled place.
“Jesus.”
In Hebrew, יֵשׁוּעַ (Yeshua)—“Yahweh saves.”
And unlike Jacob, Jesus didn’t wrestle because of sin.
He wrestled for ours.
Luke 22:44 describes Him in Gethsemane: “being in agony, He prayed more earnestly, and His sweat became like great drops of blood.”
The Greek word ἀγωνία (agōnia)—agony—carries the sense of intense struggle, like an athlete fighting to the limit.
Jesus entered the dust… not because He was a deceiver—but because we were.
He took the identity of Jacob… so we could receive the identity of Israel.
He was treated as the sinner… so we could be called sons.
This is the part that changes everything.
Jacob walked away from that night with a limp.
Jesus walked to the cross knowing it would cost Him everything.
And because of that…
Your name doesn’t have to stay what your past called you.
But here’s the truth most people avoid:
God may have already renamed you… but are you still responding to your old name?
Are you still living like “Jacob” when heaven calls you “Israel”?
Are you still hiding when grace already exposed and covered you?
Be honest.
This isn’t about information.
This is about identity.
Because someone reading your honesty might finally stop pretending too.
If this message stirred something deeper in you… not just inspiration but conviction… then step into something more intentional.
Help carry it.
Because someone is still trapped in a name Jesus already died to change.
And never forget this—
God didn’t repeat the name change because He forgot who Jacob was…
He repeated it because Jacob kept forgetting who he had become.
